findings.citation: Gabriel Lopes Cardoso and Thomas Mohaupt, "Special geometry, Hessian structures and applications", Phys. Rept. 855 (2020) 1; arXiv:1909.06240 (journal; review article)
findings.summary: A review of N=2 special geometry. Its §4 reformulates point-particle Lagrangians (a theorem of Cardoso, de Wit and Mahapatra 2013, arXiv:1206.0577, not read) so that the canonical coordinates (phi^i, pi_i) are twice the real parts of a symplectic vector (x^i, F_i), and says that canonical transformations on phase space, the Sp(2n,R) maps that include (phi, pi) -> (pi, -phi), play the role electric-magnetic duality transformations play in Maxwell-type theories; invariance under them is 'often called duality invariance'. Its §5 calls the split of the special real coordinates into x^I = Re X^I and y_I = Re F_I, the electric and magnetic components, 'the choice of a polarization'. This is, in print, the formal correspondence behind #11 §11.3: Born's rho and S-duality generated by the same matrix, and a duality frame as a Lagrangian polarization.
findings.difference: The correspondence is formal: it rewrites one particle's mechanics in special-geometry language, with the phase-space variables standing in for electric and magnetic components. It assigns no physical electric or magnetic charge to the position or the momentum polarization, puts no magnetic matter in momentum space, has no vacuum that makes both choices, and holds for any symplectic pairing, which is round 2's objection ('matrix coincidence is not physical identity') rather than support for the conjecture's physics. Useful as a checked source for the [T] half of #11 §11.3, which cites 17-dagger for the polarization language.

notes: 21 flagged papers, conjectures C2, C3, C4: 20 not relevant, 1 finding (Lopes Cardoso and Mohaupt, Phys. Rept. 855 (2020) 1, C4, related). None bears on C2 or C3: every 'monopole' on the list is a position-space object (Kaluza-Klein, H- and DFT monopoles, NS5-type backgrounds, monopole distributions, effective monopole-like forces), a mathematical analogy (Wu-Yang, stereographic device, Dirac quantization) or a reference title; none treats monopoles localized in momentum, as dark matter, or the null result of monopole searches. Method: lit.py show for all 21 abstracts; lit.py text with three grep sets (monopole terms; e-m duality terms; dark matter and Born reciprocity) for the 16 arXiv papers with HTML, each hit read in context; the 3 arXiv papers without HTML (1905.06754, 1912.07089, 2108.10297) and the 2 theses without arXiv (recid 1934108, 1827611; INSPIRE fulltext PDFs) were downloaded with WebFetch and their text extracted with pdfminer, each PDF in its own folder. Notes, grep outputs and extracted texts are in work/literature-check/round2/r2-monopoles-duality/. Screen artifact: the C4 abstract regex 's.duality' matches any word ending in s before 'duality'; two of the three C4 abstract flags here came from it (Meljanac-Mignemi 2023 'its duality'; Smolin 2015 'Born's duality'). Leads outside C2-C4, not findings: Smolin 2015 (arXiv:1503.01424) obtains Born duality X -> P, P -> -X as a remnant of an SO(1,2) symmetry of a cubic matrix model and says relativistic particles and strings follow from 'breaking that basic triality ... to a duality' by choice of compactification (quotes checked FOUND), which bears on the program's hard core (broken reciprocity), not on C1-C7; Kupriyanov, Sharapov and Szabo 2023 (arXiv:2308.07406) build Born reciprocity into symplectic groupoids and obtain a compact momentum space S^3 ('a remarkable duality between the noncommutativity of spacetime and the curvature of momentum space', FOUND), which bears on the closed-universe note's compact momentum space; Alfonsi's thesis (arXiv:2108.10297, PDF) says 'The choice of polarisation in quantisation then becomes the choice of duality frame' for T-duality in DFT, a parallel to P5's polarization language that FLM already have. The primary source of the Lopes Cardoso-Mohaupt correspondence, Cardoso, de Wit and Mahapatra 2013 (arXiv:1206.0577), was not read. The nonassociative R-flux line (Bakas-Lust, Lust-Malek-Szabo, Szabo) and Harvey-Jensen's KK monopole localized in winding space, which some listed papers cite, were assessed by workflow 1 (g2, g3) and are not repeated.
